newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Barry Callebaut sees Ivory Coast cocoa plant.
newsitem.headline: Barry Callebaut sees Ivory Coast cocoa plant.

text.p: Barry Callebaut said on Thursday it will probably build a new processing plant in the Ivory Coast to raise its cocoa processing capacity there.

Chief executive officer Pierre Vermaut told reporters in a briefing that Barry Callebaut, the world's leading grinder of cocoa beans with estimated capacity of 300,000 tonnes this year, wants to raise capacity in its plants in the Ivory Coast.
"Most probably, it will be a new plant," he said.
If constructed, it would be the fourth cocoa bean processing plant Barry Callebaut would own in the African country.
Vermaut said the company has not ruled out building another cocoa processing plant in Indonesia.
"We don't have precise plans yet, but it is not ruled out," he said.

Barry Callebaut has 19 production sites around the world. It recently opened a new production unit in Singapore with an initial capacity of 8,000 tonnes of chocolate a year. Capacity may be boosted later to 15,000 tonnes.
